_schema: Dictionary entries keyed by lowercase headword. Merged across all unit files in order; the first definition of a repeated headword wins. Examples use **bold** for the target word. Senses are ordered: the first is the flat view, the rest sit behind the full-entry toggle.

senses.en: time when you are not working or studying, and can do what you enjoy
examples: In her **leisure** time, my sister does jigsaw puzzles.
Most teenagers have very little **leisure** during exam week.
The town has a new **leisure** centre with a pool and a gym.

senses.en: the state of having time to relax, with no work you must do
senses.vi: sự nhàn hạ, sự thảnh thơi
examples: He retired early and now lives a life of **leisure**.
Read the contract at your **leisure** and sign it next week.

forms.ex: We had a **leisurely** breakfast and left at ten.

leisure.note: Usually sits before another noun: *leisure time*, *leisure activities*. The first syllable rhymes with *measure*, not with *seize*.

senses.en: something you do regularly for pleasure when you are not working
senses.vi: thú tiêu khiển, trò giải trí
examples: Fishing is his favourite **pastime**.
Board games are a cheap **pastime** for a rainy Sunday.
Collecting stamps was a popular **pastime** fifty years ago.

pastime.note: One word, one *s* — not *past time*. Close to *hobby*, but a pastime can be more casual: a hobby usually needs equipment or skill.

senses.en: to spend time somewhere, or with someone, in a relaxed way with no particular plan
senses.vi: đi chơi, la cà, tụ tập
examples: On Sundays I **hang out with** my cousins at the park.
They **hang out** at the shopping centre near the swimming pool.
We just **hung out** at home and watched films all afternoon.

senses.en: to put washing outside on a line so that it dries
examples: Could you **hang out** the washing before it rains?
My grandmother **hangs** the sheets **out** every morning.

forms.en: a place someone often goes to relax

hang out (with).note: Informal. Use *with* for people and *at / in* for places: *hang out with Nam at the café*. Irregular: hang → hung → hung.

senses.en: to meet and spend time with other people in a friendly way
senses.vi: giao lưu, gặp gỡ mọi người
examples: He loves to **socialise** with new people.
I don't **socialise** much during the week because of homework.
A club is a good place to **socialise** with people your own age.

forms.en: connected with meeting people and spending time with them
forms.vi: thuộc về xã hội, giao tiếp

forms.en: friendly and enjoying the company of others
forms.ex: He is quiet but very **sociable** once you know him.

socialise.note: British spelling *socialise*; American *socialize*. Both are correct — just be consistent. Do not confuse *social* (about society or meeting people) with *sociable* (describing a friendly person).

senses.en: to start doing a new hobby, sport or activity
senses.vi: bắt đầu (một sở thích, môn thể thao mới)
examples: I want to **take up** photography next year — I've just bought a camera.
My brother has **taken up** woodwork.
She decided to **take up** the guitar after watching the concert.

senses.en: to fill an amount of space or time
examples: That old sofa **takes up** half the room.
Homework **takes up** most of my evening.

senses.en: to accept an offer or an invitation
examples: Thanks for the offer — I'd like to **take** you **up** on it.
She **took up** the job in Da Nang.

take up.note: Separable: *take up the guitar* = *take the guitar up*. With a pronoun it **must** split: *take it up*, never *take up it*. Irregular: take → took → taken.

senses.en: do-it-yourself: making or repairing things in your home yourself instead of paying someone
senses.vi: tự làm, tự sửa chữa (đồ trong nhà)
examples: My dad spends every Sunday doing **DIY**.
She made the bookshelf herself — it was a **DIY** project.
There's a **DIY** shop at the end of our street.

DIY.note: Uncountable — never *a DIY* on its own, but *a DIY project* is fine. Say the three letters: dee-eye-**WHY**, with the stress on the last one.

senses.en: an activity in which you make things skilfully with your hands; also the objects you make
senses.vi: nghề thủ công; đồ thủ công
examples: My grandmother makes paper flowers. Her **crafts** are lovely.
We learn a traditional **craft** at school on Fridays.
The village is famous for the **craft** of silk weaving.

senses.en: a boat, an aircraft or a spacecraft
examples: Several small **craft** were sheltering in the harbour.
The landing **craft** reached the beach at dawn.

senses.en: to make something skilfully, especially by hand
examples: Each bowl is **crafted** from a single piece of wood.
She **crafts** jewellery from recycled metal.

forms.en: a skilled worker who makes things by hand
forms.ex: The chair was made by a local **craftsman**.

craft.note: In the boat sense the plural is also *craft*, never *crafts*: *three fishing craft*.

senses.en: to prepare food by heating it
examples: My dad and my brother **cook** lunch on Sundays.
The rice is still **cooking** — give it five more minutes.
My grandfather is teaching me to **cook** one new dish each week.

senses.en: a person who cooks, especially as their job or at home
examples: He is a good **cook**, but he can't stand following a recipe.
The school has two **cooks** and they feed four hundred children.

cook.note: Short /ʊ/ — the vowel of *book*, not the long /uː/ of *food*. A **cook** works at home or in a small kitchen; a **chef** is trained and works professionally.

senses.en: a shop that sells books
examples: We bought the book at the new **bookshop** in town.
A new **bookshop** opened near the swimming pool.
There is a café upstairs in that **bookshop**.

bookshop.note: British English; Americans say *bookstore*. Short /ʊ/ in *book*. Compare *library*, where you borrow books instead of buying them — a common false friend for Vietnamese learners.

senses.en: a game played by two teams of eleven players who kick a ball into a goal
examples: Last month we started playing **football** in the park.
My cousin enjoys playing **football** every Saturday.
He was too tired after the **football** match to do anything.

senses.en: the ball used in this game
examples: My little brother got a new **football** for his birthday.
The **football** went over the fence and into the garden.

football.note: *Play football* — no *the*. First vowel is the short /ʊ/ of *put*, not the long /uː/ of *food*. In American English this game is *soccer*, and *football* means a different sport.

senses.en: a game such as chess, played on a marked board with pieces or counters
senses.vi: trò chơi cờ bàn (cờ, cá ngựa…)
examples: In the evening we play **board games**.
There is a big table with **board games** upstairs in the café.
Chess is the only **board game** my grandmother ever loses.

board game.note: Two words. *Board* /bɔːd/ sounds exactly like *bored* — same sound, completely different word. You **play** a board game, but you **do** a jigsaw puzzle.

senses.en: a picture printed on card or wood and cut into many small pieces that you fit back together
examples: In my free time I like doing **jigsaw puzzles**.
This **jigsaw puzzle** has a thousand pieces and I've already lost two.
We finished the **jigsaw puzzle** on the last day of the holiday.

jigsaw puzzle.note: You **do** a jigsaw puzzle — never *play* one. Often shortened to just *a jigsaw*.

senses.en: a story told in moving pictures that you watch at a cinema or at home
examples: I usually stay home and watch **movies**.
Why don't we watch a **movie** tonight?
I can't stand any **movie** that is longer than two hours.

senses.en: the cinema, as a place you go to
examples: Do you want to go to **the movies** on Saturday?
We hadn't been to **the movies** since March.

movie.note: Long /uː/ — the vowel of *food*, not *book*. British speakers usually say *film*, and *go to the cinema* rather than *go to the movies*.

senses.en: sounds arranged in patterns to be sung or played on instruments
examples: I like listening to **music** while I do my homework.
He can't stand loud **music** when he is trying to study.
She has been studying **music** since she was six.

forms.en: a person who plays a musical instrument or writes music
connected with music, or good at music
forms.vi: thuộc về âm nhạc; có khiếu nhạc
forms.ex: He comes from a very **musical** family.

music.note: Uncountable — never *a music* or *musics*. Say *a piece of music* or *a song*. Begins /mjuː/, with a *y* sound: **myoo**-zik.

senses.en: a large structure filled with water for people to swim in
examples: Look at the blue **swimming pool** near the bookshop.
We meet at the shopping centre near the **swimming pool**.
The water in the **swimming pool** was far too cold.

swimming pool.note: *Pool* has the long /uː/ of *food*. Stress the first word: **SWIM**ming pool. Often shortened to *the pool*.

senses.en: to decide which thing or person you want from a number of them
examples: We couldn't **choose** between the film and the football match.
My mum and I **choose** the food at the market.
You can **choose** any three books from this shelf.

senses.en: to decide to do something, when you could have done otherwise
examples: She **chose** to stay at home instead of going out.
He **chose** not to answer the question.

forms.en: the act of choosing, or the thing chosen

choose.note: Irregular: choose → **chose** /tʃəʊz/ → **chosen**. Two *o*s in the present, one in the past. Long /uː/, ending in a /z/ sound.

senses.en: to rest and stop feeling worried or tense
examples: I read comics to **relax** after school.
Sunday is the only day my whole family can **relax** together.
Just **relax** — the exam isn't until next week.

senses.en: to make a rule, a muscle or a grip less tight or less strict
examples: The school has **relaxed** its rules about mobile phones.
**Relax** your shoulders and breathe slowly.

forms.en: making you feel calm — describes a thing

relax.note: Stress the second syllable: re**LAX**. Careful with the pair: a holiday is *relaxing*; you are *relaxed*.

senses.en: to dislike something very strongly; to be unable to bear it
senses.vi: không chịu được, ghét cay ghét đắng
examples: I **can't stand** loud noise when I'm reading.
My dad **can't stand** following a recipe.
She **can't stand** queuing for tickets in the rain.

can't stand.note: Always followed by **V-ing**, never *to-V*: *I can't stand queuing.* ❌ *I can't stand to queue.* The full form is *cannot stand*; *can't* is normal in speech and in most writing.
